correctness.rationale: Every genuine side of a convex polygon lies on an exposed supporting line. Samples almost surely avoid original corners, and exactly min(C_i,2) extremal sampled points on side i become hull vertices, including singleton/segment degenerate hull cases; C follows Multinomial(n,p). Product exponential GF and binomial marginal give the exact PGF and mean. For any two side probabilities at fixed total, conditioning on other occupancy and the pair total s reduces each threshold of min(B,2)+min(s−B,2) to a symmetric central interval a≤B≤s−a for B~Bin(s,u); its derivative is s*binom(s−1,a−1)u^{a−1}(1−u)^{a−1}[(1−u)^{s−2a+1}−u^{s−2a+1}], positive for u<1/2. Pair-balancing therefore increases every upper tail, and standard majorization chains prove global stochastic order. The mean summands have f_n(p)=−n(n−1)(n−2)p(1−p)^{n−3}<0 for n≥3, giving strict mean Schur concavity. For q_i=1−p_i, deficits sum to a rational function with genuine order-two poles at t=1/q_i of coefficient multiplicity*(1−q_i)/q_i>0, so expectations recover unordered side proportions and m. Independent exact multinomial/GF and two balancing examples through n≤8 agree; the analytic proof handles all admissible polygons/n, unlike finite tests.

evidence: Reitzner et al. establish facet supporting principle and expected asymptotic limit 2m, not all-n distribution or inverse reconstruction. Zubkov–Tatarenko theorem compares number of bins with at least r balls, separately, not necessarily their combined upper tails.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general order theorem for a single threshold does not establish the combined capped count without joint dependence information; nor do the asymptotic polygon mean or uniform-bin occupied count imply the rational double-pole inverse theorem.

originality.rationale: The supporting-side reduction and asymptotic limit 2m already follow from boundary random-polytope literature; individually Schur-ordered occupancy threshold counts are also prior work. The new substantive combination is stochastic order of the correlated SUM of occupied-at-least-one and occupied-at-least-two cells for every threshold, together with full inverse side-length recovery. The 2013 occupancy source was read as an accessible Russian PDF (main theorem), but specialist equivalent results remain a qualified risk.
residual_risks: A broader occupancy Schur-order theorem for nonuniform sums of capped counts may have been published under a different name; searched 2013 source establishes only individual threshold counts.
The inverse statement recovers only unordered normalized side lengths, not polygon angles, order, or shape; must not claim congruence.
